Subject: Initial APAC sizing sketch for Lighthouse (first-pass)

Team — first-pass numbers based on the forecast and assumptions below. This is a capacity planning sketch (not an offer) to drive the discovery call.

Assumptions taken:
- Peak 15-min sustained QPS estimate: 420 (combined models)
- Request mix: 65% 7B (fast), 35% 70B (slow)
- Average tokens per request (input+output): 600
- Target p95 latency <= 150ms

Sizing recommendation (Singapore region):
- Sustained pool (for steady-state and baseline latency): 20 x H100-80GB equiv GPUs
  - Rationale: expected concurrency and caching benefits on 7B models; supports continuous KV caching for having >100 concurrent sessions with <120ms median latency.
- Burst pool (for peak windows / QPS spikes): 8 x H100-80GB equiv GPUs on a separate placement group to avoid noisy neighbor effects
- Canary reserve: 4 GPUs reserved for pre-launch canary and load-tests for two weeks prior to go-live

Operational controls / policy suggestions:
- Autoscale policy: maintain sustained pool at target utilization 60-70%; allow immediate 2x burst for 10 minute windows with cooldown 5 minutes
- Model routing: route 7B traffic to GPU subset tuned for high-throughput, route 70B to GPUs with larger token cache and slightly higher per-request latency allowance
- On-call: 24/7 support for first 30 days after go-live; add SLA escalation matrix to MOP

Estimated lead time to secure dedicated GPUs in APAC: 6–8 weeks for committed pool; 2–3 weeks for burst carve-outs if we flex capacity.

I'll build a short slide with these numbers before the discovery call. LMK if we should tweak any assumptions.

— Priyom
